name: Chao Yung-Tsang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2024-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Chao Yung-Tsang is vice chairman of Jentech Precision Industrial, a supplier of cooling devices and components.
Its products are used in areas such as computers, AI servers, electric vehicles and semiconductors.
He cofounded Jentech in 1987 with older brother Chung-Hsin, now chairman of the company.
In the early stages Chung-Hsin oversaw R&D as well as business operation; Yung-Tsang took charge of finance.

name: Arthur Mensch
forbes_bio: Arthur Mensch cofounded Mistral AI in 2023 raising $113 million from investors in what was then Europe's largest ever seed round. He is chief executive.
​​The Paris-based company builds open-weight large language models that compete with U.S. rivals like OpenAI, and raised $2 billion on a $14 billion valuation in September 2025.
Mensch was born and grew up in a Paris suburb to a mother who taught physics, and a father who ran a tech company.

The French AI researcher met his future cofounder Guillaume Lample while studying at Paris' elite college École Polytechnique. Mensch would later complete a doctorate in machine learning at Université Paris-Saclay.
Mensch worked for DeepMind at its Paris office and helped work on an early version of Google's Gemini large language model before cofounding Mistral.

name: Michael Tojner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2020-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Michael Tojner bought German microbattery maker Varta in 2007 for $40 million and floated the business on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2017.
A serial entrepreneur, he has run an online gambling website, invested in real estate and hotels and has investments in other industrial companies.
He sold his entire majority stake in Aluflexpack, a flexible packaging and barrier solution company, in 2024.

name: Griffin Perry
sec_insider_companies: Fermi Inc. (FRMI) - TenPercentOwner; Granite Ridge Resources, Inc. (GRNT) - Director
forbes_bio: Griffin Perry is a cofounder of Fermi America, an Amarillo, Texas-based data center real estate investment trust.
Perry launched the firm in January 2025 with his father, former energy secretary and former Texas governor Rick Perry, and fellow billionaire Toby Neugebauer.
The cofounders took Fermi public just nine months later on the Nasdaq at a $12.5 billion valuation; Perry owns an 11% stake.
Fermi is planning to build an 11-gigawatt energy and data center campus on a 5,236-acre site in Amarillo, Texas.
Perry also serves on the board of publicly traded oil and gas exploration and production company Granite Ridge Resources.
